description: This plot illustrates the relationship between "Initial Confidence" and "Accuracy" across three different metrics, all of which include vertical error bars. The x-axis, labeled "Initial Confidence," uses a linear scale ranging from 0.86 to 1.00 with tick marks spaced at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis, labeled "Accuracy," uses a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The "Final Accuracy" metric is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers; it begins at 0.93 at x=0.86, maintains a steady, high value across the x-axis, reaches peaks of 1.0 at x=0.97 and x=0.99, and ends at 0.98 at x=1.00. The "Initial Accuracy" metric is shown as a green dash-dot line with square markers, starting at 0.64 at x=0.86, generally trending upward to a peak of 0.93 at x=0.95, dipping slightly, peaking again at 0.93 at x=0.99, and dropping to 0.77 at x=1.00. The "Δ Accuracy" metric is depicted by an orange dashed line with diamond markers, beginning at 0.29 at x=0.86, trending downward to a low of 0.05 at x=0.95, and subsequently rising to end at 0.21 at x=1.00.
